name: Ahmad ibn Idris
dom: Sufi revival; tariqa Muhammadiyya; hadith-centred mysticism
note: Moroccan reformer (d. 1837), fountainhead of the 19th-c. 'neo-Sufi' revival; teacher of al-Sanusi and the Idrisi family of orders.

name: Muhammad ibn Ali al-Sanusi
dom: Sanusiyya order; Saharan reform Sufism; zawiya network
note: Founder of the Sanusiyya (d. 1859); student of Ahmad ibn Idris; built a reformist lodge network across Libya/Sahara.

name: Sanusiyya
dom: Saharan reform tariqa; zawiya network; later Libyan state
note: Reformist Sufi order founded by al-Sanusi, rooted in the teaching of Ahmad ibn Idris; politically dominant in Cyrenaica/Libya.

name: Ahmad al-Alawi
dom: Alawiyya order; Shadhili-Darqawi mysticism; Akbari metaphysics
note: Algerian saint (d. 1934), founder of the Alawiyya, a Darqawi-Shadhili branch; subject of Martin Lings' study; influential on Western Sufism.

name: Alawiyya
dom: Shadhili-Darqawi branch; Algerian/Mediterranean spread; Western reception
note: Sufi order founded by Ahmad al-Alawi, a branch of the Darqawiyya; widely influential including on European converts.

name: Said Nursi
dom: Risale-i Nur; faith-renewal movement; Qur'anic exegesis
note: Ottoman/Turkish scholar (d. 1960), author of the Risale-i Nur; founder-inspiration of the Nurcu faith-renewal movement; Naqshbandi-influenced.

name: Nurcu Movement
dom: Risale-i Nur readers' movement; modern Turkish faith renewal
note: Faith-renewal movement of the readers of Said Nursi's Risale-i Nur; a modern Sufism-inflected community rather than a classical tariqa.

name: Ahmadou Bamba
dom: Mouridiyya order; Senegalese Sufism; sanctified labour
note: Senegalese saint Cheikh Amadou Bamba (d. 1927), founder of the Mouridiyya; Qadiri-rooted; venerated at Touba.

name: Mouridiyya
dom: Senegalese Sufi order; Touba pilgrimage; work-as-worship ethic
note: Major Senegalese Sufi order founded by Ahmadou Bamba; centred on the holy city of Touba.

name: Ibrahim Niasse
dom: Tijani revival (Fayda); West African mass Sufism; tarbiya
note: Senegalese shaykh (d. 1975), leader of the Tijani Fayda ('flood') revival; mass spiritual-training movement across West Africa and Nigeria.

name: Shaykh Hamallah
dom: Hamalliyya (Tijani offshoot); West African reform; eleven-bead litany
note: Malian Tijani saint (Ahmad Hamahullah, d. 1943), eponym of the Hamalliyya, a reformist Tijani branch repressed under French colonial rule.

name: Muhammad al-Hafiz al-Tijani
dom: Egyptian Tijani revival; hadith scholarship; tariqa renewal
note: Egyptian Tijani shaykh (d. 1978) who revitalised the Tijaniyya in Egypt and emphasised its hadith and scholarly credentials.

name: Muhammad ibn al-Habib
dom: Darqawi-Habibiyya; Moroccan Shadhili Sufism; Diwan of litanies
note: Moroccan saint (d. 1972) of the Darqawi-Shadhili line, shaykh of the Habibiyya; his Diwan is widely recited; teacher of early Western converts.

name: Hazrat Inayat Khan
dom: Chishti transmission to the West; universal Sufism; Sufi Order in the West
note: Indian musician-mystic (d. 1927), Chishti-initiated, who founded the Sufi Order in the West and introduced Sufism to Europe and America in a universalist form.

name: Pir Vilayat Inayat Khan
dom: Western universal Sufism; Sufi Order International; meditation teaching
note: Son and successor of Hazrat Inayat Khan (d. 2004); led the Sufi Order International, spreading Inayati universal Sufism in the West.

name: Bawa Muhaiyaddeen
dom: Tamil-Sri Lankan Sufism to America; Bawa Muhaiyaddeen Fellowship
note: Sri Lankan Tamil mystic (d. 1986) who founded the Bawa Muhaiyaddeen Fellowship in Philadelphia, transmitting a universalist Sufi teaching in the West.

name: Muzaffer Ozak
dom: Jerrahi-Halveti order; Turkish Sufism to America
note: Turkish shaykh (d. 1985) of the Halveti-Jerrahi order who established Jerrahi communities in North America and Europe.

name: Nazim al-Haqqani
dom: Naqshbandi-Haqqani order; global Naqshbandi spread; Cyprus center
note: Turkish-Cypriot Naqshbandi shaykh (d. 2014), head of the Naqshbandi-Haqqani order, which spread the Naqshbandi-Khalidi line worldwide including to the West.

name: Naqshbandi-Haqqani
note: Transnational Naqshbandi-Khalidi suborder led by Nazim al-Haqqani; a major vehicle of Naqshbandi Sufism in the modern West.
